September 2009 # **14****th** **– 25****th** **September 2009** # **SHFE copper inventory rises to five year high** SHFE copper stocks rose to a five year high of 104,248t on 18th September, a level not reached since April 2004. There are several reasons for the inventory jump. Firstly, copper scrap availability has eased. As the discount for scrap has widened, consumers who have the flexibility to switch between cathodes and scrap are using more copper scrap instead of cathode. Secondly, domestic cathode output is increasing, with official figures putting August production up 7.4% m-o-m to 360,047t. Finally, some invisible, off-warrant stocks are likely being released as a result of current higher prices and pushing some cathode on to the exchange. There remain significant invisible stocks in China, but the exact amount is not known. SHFE stocks subsequently fell back to 98,689t on 25th September on low level buying activity. # **Refined copper imports will continue to decline** China imported 219,731t of cathode in August, down 25% m-o-m. The decline is in accordance with the expectations of market participants. China imported huge amounts of cathode in the first half of 2009, with the positive arbitrage between SHFE and LME prices encouraging imports. However, the SHFE-LME arbitrage window closed in mid-May. The spot premium, which gives an indication of the strength SHFE inventory breaks through

The premium for imported copper cathodes is now $30-70/t, with most traders dealing at about $30-50/t. The premium for SXEW cathode is quoted at $20-40/t. CRU suspects that cathode imports will continue to decline in September and will remain low in the fourth quarter of 2009. Even the most optimistic traders do not expect the arbitrage window between SHFE and LME to reopen until December at the earliest. There is also a chance that China may start to re-export cathodes, which may displace consumption of other cathode that could end up in LME warehouses, putting downward pressure on prices. # **Demand remains stable, limited scope for further growth in 2009** In general, Chinese demand for copper has remained stable in recent weeks. Leading wire & cable producers continue to maintain a high operation rate, and tell us that they are operating at about 80% of capacity, and that their new orders are flat or increasing for the next month. The home appliance sector has seen demand fall a little due to a light consumption season and low exports. Automobile and electronic sectors have seen some recovery. Demand in the traditionally subdued third quarter has not been as weak as usual. Therefore, we believed that there is limited scope for demand to increase in the remainder of 2009. Some market insiders hope to see concrete effects of China’s RMB4 trillion stimulus plan during Q4, and it remains possible that this could offer support to the copper price in China. On balance, however, it seems unlikely that real demand will have strong enough positive momentum to drive the domestic copper price higher. # **Fundamentals may weaken in Q4** Copper scrap supply tightness in the first half of 2009 played an important supporting role in driving prices and volatility. TC/RCs in the spot concentrates market are reported to be below $10/1¢ but traders report a quiet market. Scrap availability has eased and is helping to support the recent rise in refined copper production. We assume that scrap supply will remain more abundant in Q4 2009 and certainly well above the levels seen in Q1, which should support domestic Chinese cathode output at a high level. Chinese demand also looks set to remain stable. Consequently, we expect to see imports continue to fall. © 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 3 **September 2009** www.crumonitor.com As a result, SHFE stocks are likely to continue to build and the cathode import premium looks set to remain at low levels. # **Prices likely to move sideways?** Owing to LME copper stocks increasing and American house sale data declining unexpectedly the LME 3- month dropped below $6,000/t, which is an important support level for the copper price. Tracking this downward trend, the SHFE cash price touched a one month low on 25th September at RMB46,900/t. LME and SHFE copper prices have managed to stay trading between $6,000-6,500/t and RMB 47,000-50,000/t respectively for some time. recent days, most market insiders expected that there would not be a major change in the copper price before China’s National Day since there is no trade during the festival (1st -8th October). But now that copper prices have drop below $6,000/t, it is more difficult to estimate the copper outlook in the short term. Is this the beginning of a downward trend? We do not think so yet. We believe that the copper price is most likely to move sideways, testing the RMB 46,000-47,000/t support level in the next week. However, depending on movements of the LME copper price during 1st -8th October while SHFE is closed, SHFE could see volatile trading when it reopens after the holiday. ## **Questions or comments may be addressed to:** **Grace Qu (Beijing):** +86 10 6510 2206 grace.qu@crugroup.com **John Tomlinson (London):** +44 20 7903 2103 john.tomlinson@crugroup.com This issue was completed on 25th September 2009.
